headline: Anthropic's above-range IPO collided with the worst week for tech stocks since 2020, as regulators closed in on a leaderless Nvidia and new US chip rules began to bite in China.

themes.title: Nvidia's strong quarter is swamped by probes
themes.summary: In its first report under interim CEO Colette Kress, Nvidia posted Q3 revenue of $115.8B, up 103%, and guided to $130B. Within days the WSJ reported an SEC civil probe, Reuters said it was looking at accounting, and California's attorney general subpoenaed the company over possible chip diversion to China; the shares fell about 13% on Nov 20.

themes.title: Anthropic lists into an AI sell-off
themes.summary: Anthropic priced at $83, above its $70-$78 range, opened at $111.50 and closed its Nasdaq debut at $97.17. A full greenshoe lifted gross proceeds to about $93.5B, but by Friday ANT had given back most of the pop as the Nasdaq erased its 2026 gain and the S&P 500 and Dow joined it in correction.

themes.title: US chip curbs start to bite in China
themes.summary: Commerce's Nov 16 rule requires licences for large remote access to AI compute by Chinese firms. Nvidia said it had stopped shipping licensed Hopper chips to China after $2.4B of Q3 sales, TSMC reportedly told Chinese designers to halt 16nm-and-below orders without licences, and Alibaba warned its 20 GW data-centre target may be cut.

themes.title: New frontier models and an AI maths claim
themes.summary: OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol and cut Astra's price to $8/$40 per million tokens, Google launched the $3/$15 Gemini 4 Neon for coding agents, and Alibaba formally released the 2.4T-parameter Qwen4-Max. An Anthropic mathematician also posted a Lean proof he says he and Claude found for the Riemann hypothesis; it has not yet been independently checked.
